messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open. Still, the old well in the village is running dry, and even the most patient farmers are starting to notice. Best to tend to our own fields quietly and keep an eye on the seasons ahead."*"
Sender 2: "*"The garden looks well-tended from the outside—no weeds in sight, and the fence is strong—but the gardener’s tools are rusting in the shed, and the soil beneath the roses feels strangely dry. Best to keep our voices low and our eyes open for now."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for business as usual. Still, even the most reliable forecasts can’t predict when the wind might shift, so let’s keep our ears open and our plans flexible."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Even the birds seem to be singing the same tune as the officials. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it’s best to tend to our gardens quietly."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, though the wind carries whispers of distant movement. The old walls still stand firm, but even the strongest foundations can shift if the earth beneath them trembles unseen."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms in sight, and the roads are clear. But the forecast suggests we should keep our supplies stocked and our plans flexible. Let’s stay sharp, and trust only what we see with our own eyes."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quiet, the markets are steady, and even the usual watchdogs seem distracted. But don’t mistake calm for safety; the old rules still apply, and we should stay sharp for what comes next."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s holding steady—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s shifting in ways that make the old trees creak. Best to keep your doors locked and your voices low; even the birds seem to be watching which way the branches bend."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter now—less talk of storms, more of steady skies. The trains run on time, the contracts keep coming, and even the shopkeepers seem to have put away their umbrellas. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open; the quietest moments are when the wind changes direction."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s been unusually steady this season—no storms on the horizon, but the old farmers say even the calmest fields can hide roots running deep. The harvest looks solid for now, though we all know how quickly the wind can change if the soil gives out."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard seems settled in for the long haul. Still, best to keep our plans quiet and our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts later."*"
Sender 12: "*"The usual signs are holding—noise where there should be silence, but nothing yet that can’t be contained. Still, the air feels heavier than usual, and the old rules about who watches whom seem to be shifting. Let’s keep our circles tight and our steps lighter than ever."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—less fear, more quiet agreement. The streets hum with normalcy, but the walls whisper caution. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the regime’s grip seems tighter than ever, and even the smallest misstep could draw unwanted attention."*"
Sender 14: "*"The garden looks well-tended this season—no weeds in sight, and the fence seems sturdier than ever. Even the birds are singing the same tune, though I wonder if some might be nesting quietly in the trees we can’t see."*"
Sender 15: "*"The wind has shifted—even the walls are listening more closely now. The ship’s sails are full, but the crew is trading glances, and the compass keeps spinning. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before a storm that never comes. The streets are quiet, but the walls whisper, and even the smallest cracks are being watched. Stay sharp, but keep your hands visible."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to notice. The usual signs are there, but the timing is all wrong, and the silence is louder than the whispers. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open. Still, best to keep our conversations light and our steps quiet; even calm skies can change without warning."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks calm for now, but the wind is shifting—some say the old roof might creak before it collapses. Best to keep our tools sharp and our doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather forecast is stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. Still, best to keep our plans simple and avoid unnecessary detours. Let’s meet for tea next week to discuss the usual things—work, family, and maybe that new book everyone’s talking about."*"
Sender 21: "*"Saw an interesting article about how even the most stubborn trees eventually bend in the wind—nature always finds a way to balance things out. Makes you wonder if we’re all just waiting for the right season to see what grows. Stay safe, and let’s keep our eyes open for small signs—sometimes the quietest moments hold the most truth."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls are still listening—let’s not mistake quiet for weakness. The regime’s grip may be fraying at the edges, but the machine still hums, and the elites aren’t running yet. Patience, not words, will tell us when the moment comes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. A few branches may creak, but the roots run deep, and the gardeners are tending to their plots as usual. Still, even the strongest walls have cracks, and the wind carries whispers we can’t always hear. Stay sharp, but no need to pack your bags just yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s holding steady—still sunny, but the forecast says storms might be coming later. For now, everyone’s enjoying the beach, but the lifeguards are extra vigilant, and a few smart travelers are quietly packing their bags just in case. Best to keep an eye on the horizon, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather forecast says clear skies for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s dropping. Best to keep the windows latched and the garden tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts suddenly."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
